title: Ratio: Simplest Form, Sharing and Proportion
seo_title: Ratio – Primary 5 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Express quantities as ratios; write ratios in their simplest form; share quantities in a given ratio; solve simple proportion problems. (summary of the NERDC Primary 5 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free Primary 5 maths worksheets on ratio: writing ratios, simplest form, sharing money and things in a ratio, and simple proportion. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Share: add the parts, then find one part.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • A ratio compares two amounts. 3 boys to 5 girls is written 3 : 5. The order matters.
  • Simplify a ratio by dividing both parts by the same number: 12 : 18 = 2 : 3.
  • To share in a ratio, add the parts, find the value of one part, then multiply.

Examples

Example

Share ₦12,000 in the ratio 1 : 3

4 parts, one part = ₦3,000

Answer: ₦3,000 and ₦9,000

Example

Simplify 15 : 25

Divide by 5

Answer: 3 : 5

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Writing the ratio the wrong way roundBoys to girls means boys first.
Dividing by only one partIn 2 : 3 there are 5 parts in all.
Not simplifying fully8 : 12 = 2 : 3, not 4 : 6.

faq.a: No. The order of the parts matters.
No. Both parts must be in the same unit, then the unit is dropped.

items.q: What is the ratio of circles to squares?
items.e: Count: 3 circles and 7 squares. Circles are named first, so write 3 first: 3 : 7. 7 : 3 would be squares to circles.

items.q: What is the ratio of circles to squares?
items.e: Count: 8 circles and 5 squares. Circles are named first, so write 8 first: 8 : 5. 5 : 8 would be squares to circles.

items.q: What is the ratio of circles to squares?
items.e: Count: 2 circles and 3 squares. Circles are named first, so write 2 first: 2 : 3. 3 : 2 would be squares to circles.

items.q: What is the ratio of circles to squares?
items.e: Count: 3 circles and 5 squares. Circles are named first, so write 3 first: 3 : 5. 5 : 3 would be squares to circles.

items.e: Count: 4 squares and 6 circles. Squares are named first, so write 4 first: 4 : 6. 6 : 4 would be circles to squares.

items.q: What is the ratio of squares to circles?
items.e: Count: 4 squares and 7 circles. Squares are named first, so write 4 first: 4 : 7. 7 : 4 would be circles to squares.

items.q: Which sentence is true for this picture?
c: For every 1 circle there are 4 squares.
For every 4 circles there is 1 square.
For every 1 circle there are 5 squares.
For every 3 circles there are 4 squares.
items.e: There are 3 circles and 12 squares, so circles : squares = 3 : 12. Divide both by 3: 1 : 4. So for every 1 circle there are 4 squares.

items.q: Which sentence is true for this picture?
c: For every 3 circles there are 2 squares.
For every 3 circles there are 5 squares.
For every 2 circles there are 3 squares.
For every 9 circles there are 2 squares.
items.e: There are 9 circles and 6 squares, so circles : squares = 9 : 6. Divide both by 3: 3 : 2. So for every 3 circles there are 2 squares.

items.q: Which sentence is true for this picture?
c: For every 2 circles there are 3 squares.
For every 1 circle there are 3 squares.
For every 1 circle there are 4 squares.
For every 3 circles there is 1 square.
items.e: There are 2 circles and 6 squares, so circles : squares = 2 : 6. Divide both by 2: 1 : 3. So for every 1 circle there are 3 squares.

items.q: What fraction of the shapes are circles?
items.e: There are 4 + 6 = 10 shapes. 4 of them are circles, so 410 of the shapes are circles. 46 compares circles with squares, not with all the shapes.

items.q: What fraction of the shapes are circles?
items.e: There are 2 + 5 = 7 shapes. 2 of them are circles, so 27 of the shapes are circles. 25 compares circles with squares, not with all the shapes.

items.q: What fraction of the shapes are squares?
items.e: There are 7 + 5 = 12 shapes. 5 of them are squares, so 512 of the shapes are squares. 57 compares squares with circles, not with all the shapes.

items.q: In a box, the ratio of milk chocolates to dark chocolates is 3 : 7. What fraction of the chocolates are milk chocolate?
items.e: For every 3 milk chocolates there are 7 dark chocolates, so each group has 3 + 7 = 10 chocolates. 3 of every 10 are milk chocolates: 310. 37 is the wrong fraction: the denominator must be the whole group, 10.

items.q: In a choir, the ratio of girls to boys is 5 : 2. What fraction of the children are girls?
items.e: For every 5 girls there are 2 boys, so each group has 5 + 2 = 7 children. 5 of every 7 are girls: 57. 52 is the wrong fraction: the denominator must be the whole group, 7.

items.q: In a flower bed, the ratio of tulips to daffodils is 7 : 3. What fraction of the flowers are tulips?
items.e: For every 7 tulips there are 3 daffodils, so each group has 7 + 3 = 10 flowers. 7 of every 10 are tulips: 710. 73 is the wrong fraction: the denominator must be the whole group, 10.

items.q: In a class library, the ratio of fiction books to non-fiction books is 4 : 7. What fraction of the books are non-fiction?
items.e: For every 4 fiction books there are 7 non-fiction books, so each group has 4 + 7 = 11 books. 7 of every 11 are non-fiction books: 711. 74 is the wrong fraction: the denominator must be the whole group, 11.

items.q: In an animal rescue centre, the ratio of cats to dogs is 7 : 4. What fraction of the animals are dogs?
items.e: For every 7 cats there are 4 dogs, so each group has 7 + 4 = 11 animals. 4 of every 11 are dogs: 411. 47 is the wrong fraction: the denominator must be the whole group, 11.

items.q: In a bag, 49 of the counters are red counters. The rest are blue counters. What is the ratio of red counters to blue counters?
items.e: 49 means 4 out of every 9. The rest is 9 − 4 = 5 out of every 9. So red counters : blue counters = 4 : 5, not 4 : 9.

items.q: In a car park, 27 of the vehicles are cars. The rest are vans. What is the ratio of cars to vans?
items.e: 27 means 2 out of every 7. The rest is 7 − 2 = 5 out of every 7. So cars : vans = 2 : 5, not 2 : 7.

items.q: In a bowl, 47 of the pieces of fruit are apples. The rest are pears. What is the ratio of apples to pears?
items.e: 47 means 4 out of every 7. The rest is 7 − 4 = 3 out of every 7. So apples : pears = 4 : 3, not 4 : 7.

items.e: There are 3 + 2 = 5 equal parts. One part is 20 ÷ 5 = 4. Temi gets 2 parts: 2 × 4 = 8. Do not divide 20 by 2 on its own.

items.q: Fatima and Peter share 63 marbles in the ratio 3 : 4. How many marbles does Fatima get?
items.e: There are 3 + 4 = 7 equal parts. One part is 63 ÷ 7 = 9. Fatima gets 3 parts: 3 × 9 = 27. Do not divide 63 by 3 on its own.

items.q: Dayo and Abdullahi share 45 cards in the ratio 2 : 3. How many cards does Abdullahi get?
items.e: There are 2 + 3 = 5 equal parts. One part is 45 ÷ 5 = 9. Abdullahi gets 3 parts: 3 × 9 = 27. Do not divide 45 by 3 on its own.

items.q: In a football club there are 3 times as many boys as girls. There are 36 children altogether. How many girls are there?
items.e: 3 times as many means the ratio boys : girls is 3 : 1. That is 3 + 1 = 4 equal parts. One part: 36 ÷ 4 = 9. Girls: 9.

items.q: In a swimming pool there are 4 times as many adults as children. There are 40 people altogether. How many adults are there?
items.e: 4 times as many means the ratio adults : children is 4 : 1. That is 4 + 1 = 5 equal parts. One part: 40 ÷ 5 = 8. Adults: 4 × 8 = 32.

items.q: In a box there are 5 times as many blue pens as red pens. There are 30 pens altogether. How many red pens are there?
items.e: 5 times as many means the ratio blue pens : red pens is 5 : 1. That is 5 + 1 = 6 equal parts. One part: 30 ÷ 6 = 5. Red pens: 5.

items.q: In a car park there are 3 times as many cars as bikes. There are 48 vehicles altogether. How many cars are there?
items.e: 3 times as many means the ratio cars : bikes is 3 : 1. That is 3 + 1 = 4 equal parts. One part: 48 ÷ 4 = 12. Cars: 3 × 12 = 36.

items.q: A bag has 30 beads. 25 of them are red and the rest are blue. How many blue beads are there?
items.e: 25 of 30: 30 ÷ 5 = 6, and 2 × 6 = 12. The rest: 30 − 12 = 18. (Or: the rest is 35, and 3 × 6 = 18.)

items.q: In a class of 32 pupils, 38 of the pupils have school lunch. The rest bring a packed lunch. How many pupils bring a packed lunch?
items.e: 38 of 32: 32 ÷ 8 = 4, and 3 × 4 = 12. The rest: 32 − 12 = 20. (Or: the rest is 58, and 5 × 4 = 20.)

items.q: A bag has 35 sweets. 47 of them are strawberry and the rest are lemon. How many lemon sweets are there?
items.e: 47 of 35: 35 ÷ 7 = 5, and 4 × 5 = 20. The rest: 35 − 20 = 15. (Or: the rest is 37, and 3 × 5 = 15.)

A recipe for pancakes for 4 people uses 300 g of flour. How much flour is needed for 6 people?
items.e: For 1 person: 300 ÷ 4 = 75 g. For 6 people: 75 × 6 = 450 g.

items.q: A recipe for vegetable soup for 4 people uses 600 ml of stock. How much stock is needed for 10 people?
items.e: For 1 person: 600 ÷ 4 = 150 ml. For 10 people: 150 × 10 = 1,500 ml.

items.q: A recipe for apple crumble for 6 people uses 180 g of flour. How much flour is needed for 9 people?
items.e: For 1 person: 180 ÷ 6 = 30 g. For 9 people: 30 × 9 = 270 g.

items.q: A recipe for a fruit smoothie for 2 people uses 250 ml of milk. How much milk is needed for 5 people?
items.e: For 1 person: 250 ÷ 2 = 125 ml. For 5 people: 125 × 5 = 625 ml.

items.q: A recipe for pizza dough for 8 people uses 480 g of flour. How much flour is needed for 2 people?
items.e: For 1 person: 480 ÷ 8 = 60 g. For 2 people: 60 × 2 = 120 g. Fewer people need less, so the answer must be smaller than 480 g.

items.q: A recipe for shortbread for 6 people uses 120 g of butter. How much butter is needed for 15 people?
items.e: For 1 person: 120 ÷ 6 = 20 g. For 15 people: 20 × 15 = 300 g.

items.q: Find the missing number. 7 : 6 = 42 : ☐
items.e: 7 × 6 = 42, so multiply the second number by 6 too: 6 × 6 = 36. Adding 35 to both numbers (41) does not keep the ratio.

items.q: Find the missing number. 4 : 7 = 28 : ☐
items.e: 4 × 7 = 28, so multiply the second number by 7 too: 7 × 7 = 49. Adding 24 to both numbers (31) does not keep the ratio.

items.q: Find the missing number. 8 : 7 = ☐ : 28
items.e: 7 × 4 = 28, so multiply the first number by 4 too: 8 × 4 = 32. Adding 21 to both numbers (29) does not keep the ratio.

items.q: Find the missing number. 5 : 3 = ☐ : 18
items.e: 3 × 6 = 18, so multiply the first number by 6 too: 5 × 6 = 30. Adding 15 to both numbers (20) does not keep the ratio.
